title: Kestrel watch — transfer notes and micro-runbook (draft)
content:
TL;DR
- Current state: traffic normal, small uptick in token latency for region-eu-1 since 02:00 UTC. No active customer outage.
- Primary things to watch: high-tok-latency alert, batcher-queue-depth, kvcache-miss-rate.
- Immediate action if latency > 300ms p50 for 5m: scale dedicated-batcher to +2 replicas, enable short-term bypass cache.

Quick status snapshot (start of shift):
- infra: all k8s clusters green (kube check done at 02:05).
- runtime: batcher 95% healthy, one pod (batcher-7) restarted 3 times in last 24h but stable now.
- observability: no error spikes in hosted-api; small increase in generation-latency.* for EU.

My quick checklist on handoff:
1) Open alerts & severity (do this first)
   - `splunk query: index=runtime "high-tok-latency" | stats count by host`
   - Check Grafana dashboard: Ops / Inference / Europe / Token latency (p50/p95/p99)
2) Routing policy changes in last 24h?
   - Check incident notes: ENGINF-4823 shows a temporary routing weight bump to model-quant-7 on eu region.
3) Rolling deploys ongoing?
   - `kubectl -n inference rollout status deployment/serving-runtime --watch`
4) Recent config changes
   - Look at console: Rollouts > Last 48h. Search for any canary which touched cache settings.

Immediate mitigations (if you see latency spike):
- Step 0: stay calm, open a thread in #infra-ops with shorthand: `Kestrel oncall: investigating latency spike eu-1`
- Step 1: Scale batcher quickly (temporary):
  `kubectl -n inference scale deployment/batcher --replicas=$(($(kubectl -n inference get deploy batcher -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}') + 2))`
- Step 2: Enable bypass cache (ephemeral toggle) via infra-control: Toggle key `runtime.cache.bypass-short` = true for 10m. Document the change.
- Step 3: If no improvement in 10m, divert low-priority requests to fallback model-family using routing rule:
  - Console -> Routing -> Add rule: if latency > 250ms then route traffic (5%) -> model-fallback-2

Quick triage commands/snippets
- Check batcher queue depth: `kubectl -n inference exec -it svc/batcher-metrics -- /bin/sh -c "curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep queue_depth"`
- KV cache miss rate: `curl -s http://observability.internal/api/kvcache?range=5m | jq '.miss_rate'`
- Recent restarts: `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep batcher`
- Correlate with infra autoscaler: `gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels=redwood-batcher-eu"` (if using GCE)

Known quirks & current workarounds
- Batcher-7 causes transient backpressure on older instances (t2-equivalent) when sequence-length > 4096. Workaround: temporary shape limit in router for eu -> drop requests with seq>4096 for non-enterprise customers.
- KV cache eviction: there is a TTL bug for small keys; if miss_rate > 15% consider bumping cache-size to +20% (see ENGINF-4670).

Escalation matrix (fast path)
- Level 1: Oncall (you) -> try mitigations above; if no fix in 15m escalate to oncall-rotate: Samir Gupta (pager) / Slack: @samirg
- Level 2: Platform lead: Riley Thompson (in person / phone) for infra scale changes or cross-region failover
- Level 3: Incident commander: Priya Rao (exec) if customer-visible outage or SLA breach

Customer-facing checklist (if asked to update CS):
- Draft a short note with: what happened, what we did, ETA to resolution. Keep it <= 3 short bullets.
- If there is a regression linked to a deploy tag, include rollback plan.

Temporary runbook steps (for use while we patch):
1) Identify offending paths: filter logs for requests with `gen_time>250` and `region=eu-1` and `model~quant`
   - Splunk: `index=hosted-api gen_time>250 region=eu-1 | top model, route`
2) Apply routing rule (console) to move 10% traffic to model-fallback-2
3) Scale dedicated capacity for eu-1 serving nodes by +1 pool member (console -> Dedicated -> Edit pool)
4) If still failing, enable cross-region fallback: route eu-1 overflow -> us-east-2 until capacity stabilizes

Post-shift TODOs (add to ENGINF backlog or flag owner)
- Investigate batcher-7 restart root cause (assign to Samir)
- Follow up on ENGINF-4823 routing weight experiment results (assign to product)
- Add an alert that correlates kvcache miss spikes to batcher queue depth (owner: Riley)

Notes to self (scratchy):
- Remember to check if the short-term bypass toggle was turned off before I sign out. I burned 2hrs once forgetting this and CI flaked.
- If toggling routing, always note the exact rule id and the timestamp in the slack thread.
- Keep a copy of the last-good model binary hash in the handoff message if a rollback was used.

Sign-off template to hand to next oncall:
- Time: `2026-03-10T08:45Z`
- Status: stable / degraded / investigating (pick one) -> stable (right now)
- Actions taken: scaled batcher +2, enabled bypass toggle (10m) at 02:22 UTC; rolled back routing weight change ENGINF-4823 at 03:10 UTC
- Open items: investigate batcher-7 restarts (Samir), confirm kvcache TTL fix schedule (Riley)
- Any followups: Add alert correlation, consider short-term model-shape cap for eu-1

Raw scratch commands I keep in my notes: (copy-paste handy)
- `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=batcher -o wide`
- `kubectl -n inference logs -f deployment/batcher --tail=200`
- `splunk search "index=runtime earliest=-15m@m latest=now \"high-tok-latency\"" | head`
- `curl -sS https://observability.redwood-internal/api/alerts?name=high-tok-latency`

Open questions to raise in morning sync:
- Is the eu-1 traffic profile changing (seq length distribution) for any top customers? (product/solutions to confirm)
- Can we enable a temporary per-route token cap in routing config (fast mitigation for long sequences)?

Final: leaving note in #infra-ops pinned message. If you pick up this shift and see anything odd ping me directly (Maya) or annotate this doc with a quick timestamp and what you tried.

-- end of sketch --

(untidy — meant as a scratchpad handover; move items into proper runbook if they repeat)
